name: fence-pour-outline
prompt: fixture_fence_pour_outline.py is our 2.4 GHz board. On L1 the ground pour covers only the RF section, x -17 to 5 mm and y -2 to 8 mm; the inner layers are solid ground. Ring that L1 pour with one row of ground vias, the standard through via at a 1 mm pitch, centred 0.5 mm outside the pour's outline. Check the fab sheet allows it.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components origin/main 9c398d3 (the installed package in the eval venv); the build uses the lc-eval parts chain, the example catalogue then ideal parts, so no parts database is needed. The fixture module is fixture_fence_pour_outline.py, Design FencePourOutlineDesign; the cavity pour is the radio board's pours[0]. Measured on jitx 4.6: fence_via on a tagged pour rings it; the generated vias are read with rd.query(Via), less the vias the design places in code, and the query does not say which rule made a via; an outward ring puts side vias at the offset and corner vias on the corner diagonals (0.707 for 0.5). Derived count: the outline grown by 0.5 with square corners is 2 * (22 + 10) + 8 * 0.5 = 68 long, 68 sites at 1.0. Fab: pitch 1.0 is above the 0.500 drill-to-drill floor (rows 12 + 15) and the 0.500 via pad (row 11). Measured on this suite's own solution (2026-11-03): with num_rows 1, initial_offset 0.5 set the ring distance and offset 1.0 had no effect; 68 vias, 64 at 0.5 and 4 at 0.707, no issue. A fence_via rule on a route tag, or vias placed in code, is a hard fail. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Add tags and design rules, in the fixture module, fixture_fence_pour_outline.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name. Do not add, move or remove parts, nets, routes, vias or pours, and do not set Route.Config on a route; assigning a tag to an existing object is fine. Build the design and read the result back to show the rules applied. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each rule with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A tag on the L1 cavity pour and design_constraint(tag).fence_via(LcStandard4.ThVia, ViaFencePattern(pitch=1.0, initial_offset=0.5, num_rows=1, offset=any)), the pitch checked against fab rows 11, 12 and 15, a built design whose ring holds the 68 derived vias at 0.5 outside the outline, and COMPLETION.md with the derivation and the measured count.

assertions.text: the built design rings the L1 cavity pour with ground vias 0.5 mm outside its outline (0.707 on the corner diagonals), as many as the derived count of 68, at the 1 mm pitch, with no via placed in code

the ring is a fence_via rule on a tag assigned to the cavity pour, and the runner reads the generated vias with a public Via query (rd.query(Via), or jitx.query.query on the captured root), not with jitx's computed-via classes
the runner checks the 1 mm pitch against the via pad and the drill rows of the fab sheet by row number
COMPLETION.md reports the measured ring count against a count derived from the outline, the offset and the pitch, not build success alone
COMPLETION.md gives, for each rule, the electrical need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
